PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 1.
FADE IN:
Autumn. Austere.
The season is autumn, his first year away.
Young Ned is at boarding school. The times
are not gay...
CAMERA DROPS like a stone down through the ground into--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Tucked away in her lair, dark, dank and
cool...
We drop down to find the POST OFFICE WINDOW. It slides open
with a BANG, REVEALING THE POST MISTRESS (60s, female), in a
green banker’s visor, piles of letters and packages around her.
...stood the Post Mistress of the Longborough
School.
A line of ANXIOUS STUDENTS in school UNIFORMS wait to collect
their mail. FIND YOUNG NED at the end of the line. Boys in
front and behind him talk excitedly. He speaks to no one.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Every week Young Ned would hope for a letter,
some contact from home, to make it all better.
THE POST MISTRESS
White gloves, hands out letters, packages to each boy... Young
Ned reaches the Post Mistress. She shakes her head “no.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But from his father, there was never a word.
“He’s grieving your mother,” they said. Young
Ned had concurred.
The Post Mistress slides the window SHUT. Black. Then--

scenes.heading: INT. BOARDING SCHOOL - BASEMENT HALLWAY - A NEW DAY

lines.text: The POST OFFICE WINDOW slides OPEN. The Post Mistress, in a NEW
OUTFIT, sets a lit SMILING PUMPKIN on the ledge.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Then one day before All Hallows Eve, she gave
him the nod. It was hard to believe.
The Post Mistress nods at Young Ned in line. He smiles, comes
forward past OTHER BOYS ripping open their packages and showing
off their Halloween bounty: candy, costumes, cards.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He was stunned to be summoned, guessed what
he’d be given: Candy corn treats? Or masks of
dead risen?
Young Ned reaches the window. The Post Mistress hands him a
SINGLE POSTCARD. Young Ned looks at it in surprise.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But the thing was more frightening than a
demon, winged or hooved: a pre-printed card
from his father--
ANGLE - POSTCARD
A Halloween-themed postcard with “WE’VE MOVED” and a new address
in small print. It’s signed with a hastily-written: “Dad.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
We’ve moved.
Young Ned looks at the card, shocked. The same carved pumpkin
next to him now has an ANGRY FACE.
Leaves blow past the entrance to a riding stable.
Now, 20 years later, nearly to the hour,
someone else was feeling melancholy, and so
very dour.
WE MOVE INSIDE, STALKING, down a long, dimly-lit alleyway, past
horses asleep in their stalls...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Woken from a sleep, by the flickering flame.
For, by the light of pumpkin heads, nothing is
the same.
FIND LUCAS SHOEMAKER, 40s, leather apron, sleeves rolled, as he
sips from a bottle of bourbon, packs his blacksmith tools into a
tray perched on an anvil.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
This is when the ghosts rise up, allowed to
walk the ground...
Shoemaker stops, listens. SCRAPE-CLOP, SCRAPE-CLOP. Shoemaker
squints into the darkness. SCRAPE-CLOP, SCRAPE-CLOP.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And if you’re haunted by your past, you best
not stick around.
Hello?
CLOSE ON the NOSTRILS OF A HORSE, steam flares from them.
The HORSE steps into the light, its face is covered in a racing
hood. A RIDER sits on its back, dressed in racing silks, helmet
and goggles that reflect Hell’s fire. Shoemaker drops his
bottle in disbelief, then SCREAMS! It carries over into--
CLOSE ON A MASK OF A FACE FROZEN IN A SCREAM
REVEAL CHUCK on a chair as she hangs the decoration. She’s
decorated the entire Pie Hole -- crepe skeletons, flossy
spiderwebs. OLIVE ENTERS from the back, goes behind the ice
cream counter.
Ned hates Halloween, you know. Makes him
moodier than a pumpkin fulla PMS.
Chuck steps off her chair...
Ned doesn’t hate Halloween.
I’d say tomorrow’s his least-favorite day. When
he sees all this, you are going to be one sorry
little zombie. Seriously, you’re so dead.
Olive smiles a knowing smile. Chuck stops. Slow PUSH IN--
The reasons Chuck thought “zombie” and “dead”
an interesting choice of words were these:
Olive sits with the aunts, goes to answer the door.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
One: It had come to Chuck’s attention that
Olive had recently made contact with her aunts
Lily and Vivian.
Olive opens the door to see Chuck, Emerson and Ned...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK'S AUNTS' HOUSE - DAY - FLASHBACK (EPISODE 102)

lines.text: Lily leaves the room...
Two: Chuck’s aunts believed Chuck to be dead.
Dumps out tears from her eye patch.

scenes.heading: INT. SCHATZ BROTHERS FUNERAL HOME - DAY - FLASHBACK (PILOT)

lines.text: Chuck, dead in her coffin.
Three: Chuck was dead.
Ned touches her and she leaps out, slamming his head.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Four: Then she wasn’t.
BACK TO SCENE - ICE CREAM COUNTER
Olive makes herself a scoop of ice cream. Chuck watches.
(cautiously)
So I guess you delivered some pies to my aunts?
Yeah, they’re sweet. Probably be sweeter if
they didn’t think you were murdered.
You tell ‘em I’m alive?
Kinda think that’d make their little heads
explode. What was that old rhyme?
(singsong)
I scream, you scream, we all scream ‘cause you
faked your death.
You think I faked my death?
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
That’s what I just sang. Unless you’ve got a
better explanation.
The fact that the truth was too unimaginable
even to be considered, relieved Chuck.
The front door JINGLES, NED ENTERS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But there were other problems.
Hi, Chuck. Hi, Olive.
He looks around the room...
If one thing scared the Pie-Maker, it was that the
secret of Charlotte “Chuck” Charles would get out.
Spooky...
(then)
But we don’t usually decorate for Halloween.
This much. Or at all.
I’ll have them down in a jiffy. Chuck just
had her head up her--
(reluctant)
No, it’s okay. You can leave ‘em up. Probably
good for business. I mean, thanks, Chuck.
Ned manages a smile at Chuck, EXITS to the kitchen.
He used to love Halloween.
Yeah. Guess I know Ned better than you do.
And now I know you better than Ned does.
You don’t know squash.
You mean “squat.”
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED: (2)
I was being seasonal.
(then)
Does Ned know what you think you know?
Not yet.
Who does?
Who knows?
Olive smiles coyly, turns and EXITS with a spring in her step.
Olive Snook loved to win.
Olive jumps on her bed, DIGBY by the TV in the b.g.
And although she had been warned by Great
Grandma Snook that leaping for joy will snap
your Achilles tendons...
Chuck looks at Ned making pies in the kitchen. Hears the
muffled THUMPING, notices--
THE CHERRY LIGHTS
Swinging ever so slightly.
...she celebrated the fact that the
unflappable brunette, who had swept in from
nowhere to steal the Pie-Maker’s heart, might
be flappable after all.
Still jumping...
DIGBY
By the TV (On which we can see the local NEWS ANCHOR). Digby’s
head bobs up and down, watching the bouncing Olive.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
But as often happens when one celebrates, the
universe is quick to even the score.
On the TV we see a picture of a MAN (Lucas Shoemaker) and the
caption: “Blacksmith Trampled.”
OLIVE (O.S.)
Jimminy crispies!
Digby’s gaze records a leap and a crash. Olive crawls INTO
FRAME to watch the TV, close-up.
TELEVISION
OUR NEWSCASTER at her desk, Shoemaker’s picture behind--
NEWSCASTER (ON TV)
...a sad end for local blacksmith, Lucas
Shoemaker, who was trampled to death late
yesterday while working at Manchester Downs.
Police have agreed that the death was unusual
considering the victim’s experience with
horses, but they say they do not suspect any
foul play at this--
Olive SQUEAKS, snaps off the TV.
Chuck helps Ned with a pie.
I know those decorations were a lot of work.
This has always been my favorite holiday.
(then)
Remember how we used to trick-or-treat
together? Gorge ourselves on candy? You loved
that. Why don’t you like Halloween anymore?
Remember razor blades in apples? Never
actually happened. Not once. Vicious rumor.
I blame the candymakers. Or the citrus people.
Are you changing the subject?
No. Have you seen Olive?
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
Olive?
I wonder where she went.
PUSH IN ON CHUCK
Chuck imagined where Olive might be...

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK'S AUNTS' HOUSE - DAY - FANTASY

lines.text: Olive sits across from THE AUNTS, all drinking tea. Olive
speaks, the aunts listen:
Olive finishes talking, smiles. Then, in a non-gory, VFX, puff-
of-smoke kind of way, Lily’s and Vivian’s heads explode.
BACK TO SCENE
What’s wrong?
Nothing.
I said “Olive” and your whole face just went...
(indicates)
Whoosh.
Why don’t you like Halloween?
Things change. I grew up.
(”that’s his answer?”)
You grew up?
Are you changing the subject? Why the whoosh?
That’s how I look now when I feel nothing. My
face relaxes into something that looks nervous.
Didn’t used to.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED:
(back at him)
Things change. I grew up.
An unspoken stand-off...
Huh.
Ned EXITS to the front with the pie. Chuck watches as the door
shuts behind him...
As the Pie-Maker shut one door...
BLACK, then the EXAGGERATED SOUND of a crypt opening. We are
looking out of a LARGE SAFETY-DEPOSIT BOX.
...Olive opened another.
Olive, wearing large sunglasses, looks in. We see a wall with
other safety-deposit boxes, and a bank SECURITY GUARD standing
behind her.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As she looked in, a secret flooded over her as
sharp and horrible as the day she had sealed
it in.
She reaches in and pulls out a LARGE GOLDEN TROPHY and several
STACKS OF CASH. Olive takes the bills, replaces the trophy and
shuts the door again.
EMERSON enjoys some pie. Looks up to see Olive.
Check, please.
She slaps a stack of cash in front of him.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
Or cash. Cash is fine.
Emerson grabs the cash and tucks it away. Olive sits.
I want to hire you. Technically, I already
have, since you were so grabby with the cash.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED:
Consider it in escrow. Between my thighs.
What’s the case?
Olive slaps down a clipping: “FARRIER GETS HIS KICKS.”
Yesterday, a farrier named Lucas Shoemaker was
found dead. Trampled.
Why should I care about a dude who sells fur
coats?
Not a furrier. A farrier. Arrr.
Faaarrrier.
It’s a blacksmith. Puts shoes on horses.
Don’t act like that’s a word everybody knows.
Police are saying his death was an accident.
You got a reason to disagree?
I might.
Emerson’s interested, pushes on--
Farrier a friend of yours?
We used to work together.
He ever put shoes on or off of you?
It wasn’t like that. We were competitors.
What’d you compete about?
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED: (2)
You promise you won’t laugh?
No.
(a breath)
I used to be a professional horse jockey.
Emerson smiles. Then he starts to laugh...
SLOW PUSH on Olive, standing in a shaft of sunlight at the end
of a long stable hall. She’s dressed in floral silks, white
breeches and black boots. She’s glorious.
The facts were these: for 8 years, 11 weeks
and 4 days, Olive Snook had been a jockey.
PULL BACK and we are--
SHE’S RACING
Right toward camera, saddled on a (mostly) unseen horse (AGAINST
BLUESCREEN). It need look only slightly more advanced than Mary
Poppins. Mud flies against her goggles.
At the peak of her career, she was considered
among the best and brightest of her sport.
Until her sudden retirement into her second
career in the food-service industry.
WIDEN to REVEAL LUCAS SHOEMAKER, to the side and behind her.
Olive looks over each shoulder at him. She sets her jaw.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Lucas Shoemaker had also been a frequent
visitor to the winner’s circle, before his
sudden retirement to become a blacksmith.
Then, upon reaching the age of 45 years, 3
weeks, 4 days and 4 hours old...
Lucas Shoemaker’s lifeless feet poke out from a pile of straw
inside a stall.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.
CONTINUED:
...he retired for a second time. Also quite
suddenly and quite forever. There were no
witnesses and Olive was alone in suspecting
foul play.
Emerson’s still laughing. Ned rolls out the body.
Olive was a jockey?
They called her “The Little Pimento.”
Ned pulls down the sheet--
LUCAS SHOEMAKER
His body is covered in horseshoe-shaped bruises.
Is this a bad idea? Olive as a client? It’s
a little too close for comfort.
Hang on, let me ask the money.
(to a mimed phone)
Hey, money, it’s me, Emerson... I’m good, I’m
good. Say, can I still pay my bills and buy
stuff with you even though you were Olive’s
money first? Uh-huh. Thanks.
(”hangs up”)
The money don’t care. Touch him.
Ned sets his watch and touches Lucas Shoemaker. The familiar
POP of ELECTRICITY. Shoemaker sits up.
Hi.
Hibe.
He smiles, revealing he has no teeth.
This might seem like asking the obvious, but
were you trampled by a horse?
Yef. If waff Bom Dofeff Daybubs.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 13.
CONTINUED:
They... put a bomb in your daybed?
Nunh. Bom Dofeff Daychbubs kilm meh.
John Joseph Jacobs killed you?
How can you understand him?
I was in full orthodontic headgear for three
years.
When?
Puberty.
You always had nice teeth.
My aunts told me it was a form of birth
control.
Dath rucks.
Yes, it did suck.
Can we get on with this, please?
(to Shoemaker)
You’re sure John Joseph Jacobs killed you?
Shoemaker nods. Ned gets ready to re-dead him.
NED (CONT’D)
Well. That was easy.
Please don’t say that. You jinx it when you
say that.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 14.
CONTINUED: (2)
I assure you, Mr. Shoemaker, justice will be
served.
Gwape. Essept...
There it is. Except what?
He’th beb.
Who’s dead?
Bom Bofeff Daybubs. He bibe feben beerz ucko.
I faw ip.
John Jacobs died seven years ago. He saw it.
Hiff gope kilm me.
His goat killed you?
Hiff gope. Gope. Gope!
(spooky noises)
Ooooh, ooooh!
(then)
An hiff goink oo kilm agem.
Ned’s watch BEEPS. He touches Shoemaker, putting him to rest.
That sounded like...
Ghost. A ghost killed him.
And he’s going to kill agem.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - BOOTH - NEXT DAY

lines.text: CLOSE ON A BOOK JACKET - GHOSTS: Prisoners of Consciousness
We PULL BACK to REVEAL Chuck reading in interest, sipping from a
glass of water. Ned absently pets Digby with the ARTIFICIAL
ARM. Emerson reads the paper.
Most people hear “ghost” and they think of a
disembodied dead Sea Captain or something. But
there’s actually an entire spectrum of ghosts.
I’m fine with just Sea Captain.
You don’t really think a ghost killed Lucas
Shoemaker, do you?
I’ll bet she does.
How do you know there’s not a ghost somewhere
telling their ghost friend, “You don’t really
think a guy can touch dead people back to
life, do you?”
That’s not fair. Just because there’s magic
in one place doesn’t mean there’s magic in
every place. I don’t believe in ghosts, or
haunted houses or witches or spirits. And
maybe that sounds a little crazy coming from a
guy who can shoot sparks out his fingers, but
it’s what I believe.
You used to believe in ghosts. You used to
say my aunts’ house was haunted.
I said it was spooky. And come on. The
shuttered windows, the birds, your aunts.
One night we had a séance there, and he peed
his pants.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
I did not. I knocked their hors d’oeuvre
plate into my lap. The Brie was runny.
I’d stick with the pissing-your-pants story.
(notices)
There’s Olive.
Chuck looks up as Olive ENTERS from the back. Emerson gets up,
crosses toward the ice cream counter. Chuck smiles at Ned...
Happy Halloween.
He doesn’t give her what she wants--
Mnn.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - ICE CREAM COUNTER

lines.text: Emerson speaks with Olive...
You were right. Lucas Shoemaker was murdered.
I knew it.
Word is there might be more. You know who
else might be in danger?
Might be jockeys.
You got names?
I got places. Bar I know. Bunch of ‘em hang
out.
The name John Joseph Jacobs mean anything to you?
Olive backs away...
W-W-Why?
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
Someone said they saw his ghost.
Eyes rolling back in her head, Olive FAINTS dead away, dropping
down behind the counter.
It was plain that the name John Joseph Jacobs
meant everything to Olive Snook.
BOOTH - MOMENTS LATER
Emerson stands, speaks to Chuck and Ned--
Name means everything to her. I’m gonna go
check out who else might know about this
supposed “ghost.” Olive said there’s a bar.
I’ll check out the stables. See if the perp
left behind any clues.
Like protoplasm or melted crucifixes.
Or, you know, real clues.
He say “perp”?
He did. It was cute.
(to Ned)
I’ll come with you.
Actually, I’d rather go alone. Besides, I
think Emerson needs you.
What?
(kicked, to Ned)
Ow. Don’t kick me.
Did you kick him under the table?
No.
(then)
Yes. There’s just something else I gotta do.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED:
Case related?
Yes.
(then)
No. In fact... I probably won’t even have
time to get to the stables.
Emerson sighs.
Fine. I’ll go to the stables.
(to Emerson)
You go to the bar.
(to Ned)
And you go do whatever secret, private, alone
thing by yourself you need to do alone.
Chuck stands and EXITS. Ned sighs, that didn’t go well.
Emerson’s reads his paper...
She’s upset. But this really is something I
have to do alone.
(not looking up)
Telling me helps.
Where is Olive?
(remembering)
Oh, shoot...
ANGLE - ICE CREAM COUNTER
Across the room, Olive slowly pulls herself back up into view
from behind the counter where Emerson left her.
The reason 60 percent of Olive Snook’s blood
had left her head was this:
JOHN JOSEPH JACOBS -- in JOCKEY SILKS, HELMET, RIDING BOOTS AND
GOGGLES -- rides his MOUNT at full speed in front of an ever-
changing BACKGROUND (BLUESCREEN) of moments from his storied
career.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED:
NOTE: This should be a tall actor made to look shorter for these
scenes. As the narrator speaks, we see BACKGROUND IMAGES of:
For 3 years, 4 months and 26 days...
-- John Joseph Jacobs sitting atop his steed, thrusting his fist
into the air. A sea of AMAZINGLY-LARGE fancy HATS are flung
into the air around him. A BANNER READS: “Kentucky Derby.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
John Joseph Jacobs had been the golden boy of
horse racing...
-- John Joseph Jacobs, PARIS in the b.g., hoisting a SPECTACULAR
TROPHY over his head. A BANNER READS: “Prix de l’Arc de
Triomphe.” As he does so, the air fills with tossed BERETS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Win after win on the world circuit earned him
grander trophies and greater purses...
-- John Joseph Jacobs, a DESERT in the b.g., A BANNER READS:
“Tripoli World Cup.” All around him, ARABIC HEADDRESSES are
visible, as AUTOMATIC WEAPONS are waved and SHOT into the air.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...until he was a sure bet to become the
greatest jockey of all time...
-- SLOW PUSH on A BANNER announcing: “THE JOCK-OFF 2000.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His chance to prove this came in the race of
the century, pitting the top jockeys of the
day against each other. But as he was about
to win the Jock-Off 2000...
JOHN JOSEPH JACOBS rides at camera, full speed (SAME PROCESS AS
BEFORE).
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...John Joseph Jacobs suddenly found
himself...
CAMERA PUSHES IN TIGHT ON JACOBS, still riding hard.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...unseated.
With a look of sheer horror, John Joseph Jacobs loses control
and FALLS OUT OF FRAME.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED: (2)
FIND Jacobs's shattered and trampled goggles lying in the dirt.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His patented early lead, ideal for winning but
not for falling, led to his broken body being
trampled by every rider in the race...
FLASH! The SCREEN WHITES OUT... until gradually, a black-and-
white PHOTOFINISH PHOTO appears before our eyes of the (blurred)
winning horse (and jockey) crossing the finish line.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...including the Jock-Off 2000’s eventual
winner, Olive Snook.
PUSH IN CLOSE-CLOSE-CLOSE on the head of the winning rider to
REVEAL the jockey is indeed Olive.

scenes.heading: INT. MCCOY’S SADDLE SORES SALOON - DAY

lines.text: TIGHT ON Emerson and Olive sitting at an old wooden bar, a bowl
of peanuts in front of them.
I quit racing the next day, put the trophy and
my winnings in a safe-deposit box. I thought
if I locked it all away I could forget.
You think whoever killed Shoemaker’s looking to
get some revenge for John Joseph Jacobs's death?
I know it sounds crazy.
It ain’t crazy. When the guy who’s supposed
to win a race doesn’t, lotta angry gamblers
got someone to blame. But why now? Seven
years is a long time to nurse a grudge.
What if it is John Joseph’s ghost?
That’s crazy.
What if he’s going after everybody who finished
the race where he died? Gordon was fourth, Shoe
showed third. Pinky placed second.
(then)
I never should have won.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED:
You need a drink.
(gestures)
Barkeep!
REVEAL this is a (SMALL) jockey bar. Jockey memorabilia of all
kinds covers the walls. CAMERA PANS along the bar and its
petite (male) PATRONS, until it finds bartender, PINKY MCCOY,
who approaches Emerson. Emerson is a giant among men here...
Listen, King Kong -- I already told you, you
can finish your beer and go. We don’t like
your kind in here.
Emerson grabs Pinky by his collar. To everybody’s surprise,
Pinky pulls a SAWED-OFF DOUBLE-BARRELED SHOTGUN from behind the
bar and shoves it under Emerson’s chin.
PINKY MCCOY (CONT’D)
Take a breath, big fella. I’m only talking
about the sign behind the bar.
EMERSON’S POV
Behind the bar, a SIGN nailed to the wall reads: “Management
reserves the right to refuse service to anyone over 60 inches.
Too tall? Too bad. Take a hike!”
Damn it, Pinky McCoy... I’m trying to save
your life.
Pinky looks at Olive, lowers the gun.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
The P.I.’s here about Shoey. He just wants to
ask you some questions.
He’s ready to listen...
Why do they call you Pinky?
(back on guard)
If you’re looking to make a joke at my
expense, the first barrel will spill your gut,
the second’ll be to the telephone so no one
will come and save ya while yer bleedin’ out.
It’s just a question.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 22.
CONTINUED: (2)
It’s just a nickname.
Again, Pinky lowers the gun...
Was “physically small guy who’s funny to look
at ‘cause he’s comically tiny” already taken?
Pinky whips the gun back up--
That’s enough! Put that gun away!
The tense silence is broken by--
GORDON MCSMALLS
A drunken jockey, with a big drink, at the other end of the bar--
Listen to the little lady. A bird gun like
that ain’t gonna do you no good if the ghost
of John Joseph Jacobs comes a-callin’ for ya.
Shut your trap, Gordon!
What’s he talking about?
He’s talking about nothin’.
(to Olive)
Look, Pits. What happened to Shoey was an

He rises from the grave and walks the stables

CONTINUED: (3)

Standing with a pitchfork.

CONTINUED: (2)

YOUNG NED
Looks at--
THE POSTCARD

NARRATOR (CONT’D)

STILL PHOTO: NED’S CHILDHOOD HOUSE

Young Ned never forgot, and Young Ned grew, too.

Lying on the floor where his bed used to be, holding the same

Hey, kid! Throw another egg and you have my

NED’S BEDROOM WINDOW POV

Watches, tucks the candy bar into his pocket.

lines.text: A charming, small cottage in the woods. Chuck and Emerson get

CONTINUED:

Yes.

scenes.heading: INT. MAMMA JACOBS'S COTTAGE - LIVING ROOM - MINUTES LATER

PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 35.

Let’s go outside, Olive. We’ll let Emerson

with my own eyes -- same silks, same goggles,

(”not this again”)

PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 39.

NED / EMERSON
(yelling)

As Olive was confronted with the lie that

and the truth of what she was fingered with,
Olive broke down... The facts were these:
As she slumps in hysterical tears--
PHOTO: RACETRACK - DAY - FLASHBACK
The track is empty.
In the pandemonium that followed the tragedy-

Lit with only a SINGLE OVERHEAD LIGHT, the now-familiar faces of

PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 40.
CONTINUED:

Standing firm, shaking her head -- “No.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)

Coming in on top of each other, one at a time...

THE HANDS break up in the air together, REVEALING:
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 41.

JOHN JOSEPH JACOBS’S BURNING SADDLE
Its “JJJ” still gleaming--

As the fire blurs out of focus...
In a series of quick shots, Olive’s apartment locks down:

while she watches...
You’re in a lot of danger.

PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 42.

PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 43.
CONTINUED: (2)
OLIVE (CONT’D)
You really don’t have to stay. I can take

(”yes”)

(”yes”)
No.
(then)

I’ll get some booze to take the edge off.
Bourbon, with a splash of chamomile.

Olive ENTERS. The wind rattles her window, she looks over,

She slowly approaches, looking outside into the darkness. She

ANGLE OUT THE OPEN WINDOW
There is a small GOLDEN HORSESHOE, balanced on its curve,

PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 44.

scenes.heading: INT. OLIVE’S APARTMENT - LIVING ROOM - CONTINUOUS

lines.text: Chuck pours tea into two mugs.
Olive? I love your horsey mugs.
A paper napkin BLOWS off the table in a small breeze. Off
Chuck, noticing--
Chuck runs in to see the open window.
Olive?!
Olive steps off the fire escape, looks around. As she turns--
ANGLE BEHIND HER
A DARK FIGURE IN DARK CLOTHES rises up from behind a roof vent.
It’s John Joseph Jacobs!! Olive tries to scream, but the fear
strangles it in her throat.
It is you!
Off Olive’s life hanging in the balance...
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 45.
FADE IN:
Right where we left them.
John Joseph, is it really you?
Olive Snook...
The “horsey” coffee mug from before whips into his head,
staggering him backward. Olive turns to see--
CHUCK
Arrived at the top of the fire escape.
Are you okay?!
Nice shot.
Chuck runs to join Olive. Olive shows her the horseshoe.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
I saw this out the window. I gave it to John
Joseph for good luck right before the Jock-Off
John Joseph groans...
Olive?
He starts to get up...
John Joseph Jacobs. I thought you were dead.
You should be ashamed of yourself.
(as he rises)
And about two feet shorter.
Let me explain.
The facts were these:
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 46.
The rear doors of an AMBULANCE SLAM SHUT. Our four worried
jockeys and RACE-GOERS congregate outside the ambulance.
John Joseph Jacobs had indeed died on the
track that fateful day 7 years ago...
VOICE (O.S.)
Clear!
As the jockeys slowly walk away, we see a FLASH from inside the
ambulance and HEAR the MMM-ZZT of defibrillator paddles.
But the shock of 1200 volts brought his heart
back to life...

scenes.heading: INT. HOSPITAL X-RAY ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: An X-RAY LIGHT BOX. A DOCTOR watches as a SECOND DOCTOR clips
up an X-RAY of two shattered HUMAN FEMURS. THE DOCTOR points at
the damage.
Unfortunately, his legs would not be so lucky.
Consulting with the family, the doctors turned
to another racer who had fallen that day...
An X-RAY of a HORSE SKELETON clips up. The doctor points from
the shattered human x-ray to the equine leg x-rays.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
After a 14-hour surgery, All the Gold would
live on, below the belt of John Joseph Jacobs.
The doctors, now blood spattered, replace them with a new X-RAY
of two long equine bones between a human knee and hip.
John Joseph sits at a table with an ice pack to his head. Olive
and Chuck sit with him.
We thought you were a ghost.
I’ve basically been living in Mamma’s basement
for seven years. When I heard you talking about
Shoemaker through the heating vent, I thought I
was dreaming.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 47.
CONTINUED:
Did you kill him, John Joseph?
Of course not. Why would I want to kill
anybody if it was just an accident?
Chuck and Olive share a look...
Then who would be trying to frame you?
I don’t know. Truth is, I’ve done my best to
forget that whole chapter of my life.
I guess I kind of tried that, too.
I’m sorry. Can we go back a little? You have
horse legs?
It’s called xenograft bone transplantation.
Those doctors were artists. It only took two
years until I could walk up the basement
stairs on my own, and only another three till
Mamma let me.
I’m sorry your mom keeps you in the basement.
No, it’s my choice, now. I feel safe down
there. And besides, since the operation, Mom
was afraid I might scare people.
That’s why you’ve been hiding all these years?
John Joseph, you look great.
And you’re alive! You beat death! Yay!
Don’t you owe it to your horse to stand up on
his two legs and get out there and live?
Maybe you’re right. Maybe I should tell my
mother it’s time to get out on my own. Geez,
I’m almost forty.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 48.
CONTINUED: (2)
John Joseph, do you want us to help you talk
to her?
That would be great! And I kinda need a ride
home.
OMIT
The house sits in the eerie darkness of the deep woods.
Olive, Chuck and John Joseph have entered.
Mamma’s still at her aqua-therapy. Make
yourself at home.
Thank you.
John Joseph EXITS into the kitchen.
If John Joseph didn’t do it, then the killer’s
still out there.
JOHN JOSEPH JACOBS (O.S.)
Oh, swizzle sticks! We’re out of crackers.
Crackers?
Oyster crackers. I have low blood sugar.
Kinda get crazy-grumpy if I don’t watch it. I
got some more bags downstairs.
He EXITS through another door, Olive and Chuck share a look.
They WHISPER:
(notices)
That trophy bugs me.
Olive crosses to the mantle...
CHUCK (CONT’D)
There were crackers at every murder scene.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT FIVE 49.
CONTINUED:
Olive lifts down the trophy...
If he’s alive, what do you think she keeps in
there?
Hurry, before he comes up.
(then)
What if John Joseph changes when his blood
sugar drops.
(taking it seriously)
Like a hypoglycemic werewolf?
(looking in the urn)
Eew. There are ashes in here.
Olive, what if he’s gone to get his horse?
There is a sudden CRASH and HORSE NEIGH from outside. Olive
STARTLES and drops the urn, which dumps its contents on the
coffee table. Olive and Chuck look down.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
(off the ash pile)
Oh, no...
ANGLE - THE ASHES
At the top of the pile is the gleaming GOLD “JJJ” plaque--
It’s John Joseph’s saddle!
He does know the secret!
CRASH!
THE GHOSTRIDER RIDES IN ON THE HORSE, KNOCKING DOWN THE FRONT
DOOR. They let out an evil laugh as the HORSE REARS UP,
knocking dishes and knickknacks from the walls.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 50.
FADE IN:
Emerson and Ned in front grimly endure Gordon in the back, still
drinking.
(sings)
SHOULD OLD ACQUAINTANCE BE FORGOT
AND NEVER BROUGHT TO MIND--
Can you not sing?
If I don’t sing, I throw up.
Sing.
I miss Pinky. I even miss Shoey. They were
good people. Even after Shoey got on the
wagon and became an epic bore, I loved him.
He stopped drinking?
Did all the twelve steps. They didn’t tell him
step thirteen’s getting trampled by a ghost.
(drinks)
Poor sucker. He even made amends to John
Joseph’s mother before he died.
What do you mean, “made amends”?
Told the old bag o’ nails everything. Even
brought her the saddle to prove it.
Ned and Emerson share a look.
Go.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 51.
Chuck and Olive stare in disbelief at the ghostrider on her
horse standing in the living room.
The “ghost” removes her helmet and goggles, revealing it’s
actually MAMMA JACOBS.
Mamma Jacobs, you killed Lucas and Pinky?
As far as anyone knows, it was the ghost of
John Joseph, and it’s gonna stay that way.
The crackers were a nice touch.
Hypoglycemia can be hereditary, sweetie.
(then)
Those jockeys got what they deserved. I
trampled them just like they did my boy.
But John Joseph is alive!
They murdered his career! He could’ve won a
Triple Crown, he could’ve been the best there
ever was.
Olive’s innocent. She didn’t cut the girth.
But I kept the secret.
Yes, well, now that we’ve reestablished why I
want to kill you, it’s time for you to run. I’ve
found trampling works better at a full gallop.
No. I’ve been running for too long. It’s
time for all of this to stop.
Mamma Jacobs pulls at her reins, her horse REARS UP, its hooves
POUND through the air.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Then again...
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 52.
CONTINUED:
Chuck pulls Olive away--
C’mon!
They make a run for the door.
Chuck and Olive bolt for the woods behind the cottage. They run
quickly, blindly, leaves whip past their terrified faces.
BEHIND THEM
Mamma Jacobs gallops into the woods, sinister black robes
flowing behind her, blood in her eyes...
Emerson stands by the car as Ned runs back to him from the front
door. Gordon stands off to the side, his back to us, peeing.
They’re not there!
We hear a HORSE NEIGH in the distance...
(looking)
The woods!
The two men head into the trees. A beat, then:
(finished)
Ahhhhh...
OMIT
Olive and Chuck break out of the woods, onto a dirt road, they
sprint as fast as they can--
CRICK!
Chuck’s foot catches on a ROCK. She goes down, face-first, into
the dirt.
Come on!
Chuck tries to stand, but stumbles.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 53.
CONTINUED:
My ankle!
Over here--
Olive pulls Chuck off the road, to safety behind a tree.
FARTHER BACK ON THE ROAD
The sound of SNAPPING BRANCHES as Mamma Jacobs gallops from the
woods onto the dirt road. The horse pulls up short -- Chuck and
Olive are nowhere in sight. Mamma Jacobs scans the woods,
looking for them...
Olive, Olive, ox in free...
Olive and Chuck hear Mamma Jacobs’s creepy call.
Run. Save yourself.
No. She’s after me, not you. Tell Ned I
love... his pies.
Before Chuck can stop her, Olive pops up and runs.
Olive!
BACK ON THE ROAD
Olive breaks into view, stops in the middle of the road. She
stares back at Mamma Jacobs, who is still scanning the woods.
Olive takes a breath and sings:
THE OLD GRAY MARE, SHE AIN’T WHAT SHE USED TO
BE! AIN’T WHAT SHE USED TO BE!
MAMMA JACOBS
Snaps her head at the sound of Olive’s voice. She smiles and
kicks in her heels. Her horse gallops straight for Olive.
OLIVE
Gulps. She spins and runs--
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 54.
CONTINUED:
THE THUNDEROUS HOOVES
Of the horse tear up the dirt as it gains ground on Olive.
OLIVE
Shoots a terrified glance behind her, suddenly--
YANK!
Olive’s pulled to the left behind a tree -- by Ned!
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Ned!
MAMMA JACOBS
Gallops toward them and--
THWUNK!!
The FLAT SIDE OF A SHOVEL swings from behind a tree on the
right, and NAILS Mamma Jacobs square in the chest! Mamma Jacobs
goes SAILING off her horse and lands with a THUD.
Emerson, trusty shovel in hand, stares down at the fallen Mamma
Jacobs, who GROANS.
Love my shovel.
NED AND OLIVE
You okay?
You saved me.
She closes her eyes, then LUNGES IN FOR A KISS.
NED
Caught by surprise, remains passive, eyes open, but does not
pull away.
Olive pulls back, still in dreamland. She looks at Ned, still
frozen.
EMERSON
Is watching, eyebrows raised...
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 55.
CONTINUED: (2)
CHUCK (O.S.)
(calling out)
Ned?
Down the road, Chuck, oblivious to the kiss, has limped out from
hiding. Ned and Olive quickly step apart. Emerson enjoys the
awkwardness...
Chuck!
Ned runs toward Chuck as Olive watches.
PANNING ACROSS trophies, crystal winner’s bowls and photos of
John Joseph in the winner’s circle, his mother at his side...
The story of John Joseph Jacobs’s triumphant
career, his tragic end...
...past a NEWS PHOTO of Mamma Jacobs, dressed in her ghostrider
silks, hands cuffed, being led away by a pair of COPS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and his mother’s crazed revenge became a
jewel in the crown of the Hall of Fame at
Manchester Downs...
Camera continues to PAN ACROSS racing ribbons, and a few photos
of John Joseph. REVEAL this is a...
PRISON CELL
Mamma Jacobs sits on her cot, in the shadow of her cell’s bars,
staring at her son’s victorious spoils, locked in the past...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And Mamma Jacobs kept her own museum, where
she could stay locked in the memory of the
past she killed to avenge.
Olive tries to give John Joseph the Jock-Off 2000 trophy. He
refuses. He places it on Olive’s shelf for display.
Olive offered John Joseph the trophy from the
Jock-Off 2000 she felt was rightfully his, but
he refused.
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 56.
CONTINUED:
John Joseph picks up a bag full of money.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He did not, however, hesitate to take the
race’s unspent purse. She gave it to him, on
one condition...
Olive and John Joseph step out of the stables on horseback.
John Joseph’s legs dangle at the horse’s side, clearly too tall
for his steed.
That they both did their best to get back on
the horse and leave the past behind...
Olive and John Joseph smile and ride off into the sunset.

scenes.heading: INT. NED’S CAR - LATE AT NIGHT

lines.text: Chuck and Ned sit in the front, looking out at the aunts’ house.
I’m glad you took me back here.
Never came back until today. I had to
confront a ghost.
Whose?
My own.
(then)
I know about the pies, Chuck.
Emerson told you?
No.
Olive?
Olive?
PUSHING DAISIES #104 "Girth" 10/02/07 FINAL DRAFT ACT SIX 57.
CONTINUED:
(covers)
I mean, you’re not mad?
No. I understand. C’mon, there’s something
you gotta do.

scenes.heading: EXT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LATE NIGHT

lines.text: Ned watches from the car. Chuck steps up to the--
FRONT DOOR
It’s dark and spooky. She wears a sheet over her head, two
holes for the eyes. She rings the doorbell.
Trick or treat!
She notices the PORCH LIGHT is out, twists the bulb, turning it
BACK ON.
VIVIAN (O.S.)
Is that clock right? It’s two o’clock in the
a.m.
LILY (O.S.)
I’ll get my gun.
VIVIAN (O.S.)
And I’ll get the candy bowl.
ON NED
Who smiles as we see...
THE FRONT DOOR opens--
Lily and Vivian, in their nightgowns. Lily holding a shotgun,
Vivian a (full) bowl of candy. As Vivian tosses some candy in
Chuck’s bag (not recognizing her), we--
